messages:
mira: Heads-up — e2e perf run after the kv-cache kernel selection patch shows a reproducible ~12% increase in p99 for medium-length (512) chat workloads. p50 unchanged. Full run output: https://perf.redwood/reports/175825

sam: thanks, Mira. do we have the exact commit + model used? and is this synthetic replay or live traces?

mira: commit a3f9c2d (kv-cache selector refactor). Model: llama-2-13b, 512 seq, batch sizes 1/4/16. This was synthetic replay of production traces (captured last week).

devin: quick question on methodology — are we aggregating p99 across shards or taking max(p99) per shard? that can move numbers a lot.

mira: we currently compute tail by aggregating all request latencies and taking the 99th percentile global. Suspect this hides per-GPU skews.

orla: for regression triage we usually look at per-shard p50/p95/p99 and also the max-p99. we should report both. Also confirm warmup and steady-state windows.

mira: warmup = first 30s excluded, steady-state = next 5m. Ran each test 3x. raw numbers (global p99): baseline 78ms -> new 87ms. p50 22ms -> 23ms. throughput stable.

ana: first-pass sanity — could this be KV cache miss amplification? the selector might be choosing kernels with worse amortized KV handling.

devin: agree. Also need to check sequence-length distribution skew — if selector recompiled kernels targeting longer contexts we might see worse perf on 512.

mira: good points. I diffed the kernel selection table; the patch added a heuristic preferring fused-attn kernels on some shapes. I can paste the selection map: `{"seq":512,"batch":1} -> fused-attn-v2 (was fused-attn-v1)`

sam: can you run microbenchmarks for the two kernels? isolated throughput + tail latencies per kernel for the same shape. use bench/kern_bench.py with --iters 2000 --concurrency 16 to hit tail.

mira: running that now. perf-bot will post when done.

perf-bot: [auto] microbench results uploaded: https://perf.redwood/artifacts/175825/kern_bench.json (kv-cache-enabled, 512, b=1, conc=16). Summary: fused-attn-v2 p99=92ms, fused-attn-v1 p99=78ms, throughput within 3%.

a na: that matches the regression. can we capture hardware counters? maybe the new kernel spills more or has worse memory access patterns under KV.

devin: also sanity-check correctness — run token-level logit-diff between kernels for a small prompt to ensure no behavioral change. script: ```python
# quick check
out1 = run_model(kernel='fused-attn-v1', prompt='...')
out2 = run_model(kernel='fused-attn-v2', prompt='...')
assert max(abs(out1.logits - out2.logits)) < 1e-4
```

orla: for triage steps, propose: 1) repro microbench (mira) 2) hw counters + flame graphs (devin) 3) correctness check (ana) 4) rollback patch or gate kernel selection (sam) if confirmed. owners assigned?

mira: I'll own (1). started the microbench run.

devin: I'll collect perf counters (L2 misses, DRAM BW) and flamegraph CPU/GPU. Also run with nvprof.

ana: I'll run the logit diff tests across a handful of prompts and add token-level divergence metrics to the CI check. if we see >1e-3 divergence we treat as behavioral change, else perf-only.

sam: temporary mitigation: add a config toggle to prefer v1 for seq<=1024 until we finish triage. small PR ready, but holding until microbench confirms.

mira: microbench confirms numbers and uploaded traces: https://perf.redwood/artifacts/175825/trace.tar.gz. I'll also attach a per-shard p99 heatmap.

perf-bot: [auto] nightly regression alert created: RG-2025-175825. Triage board: https://kanban.redwood/rg-2025-175825

orla: ok, action items and timeline? we should aim for 24-48h turnaround for triage with rollback if behavioral regression confirmed.

devin: ETA 8h for perf counters + flamegraphs.

ana: ETA 6h for logit diffs across 10 prompts.

mira: ETA 3h to validate selection heuristics and push a revert toggle.

sam: I'll prep the rollback PR and set canary to v1 for the impacted lanes.

orla: please paste the exact bench command you used (so QE/devs can reproduce). also include randomness seeds and docker image tag.

mira: bench command: `./bench/kern_bench.py --model llama-2-13b --seq 512 --batch 1 --concurrency 16 --iters 2000 --kv-cache --seed 42 --image redwood/infer:2025-11-12-a3f9c2d`

sam: perfect. one more note on methodology: let's standardize reporting to include per-shard max-p99, global-p99, p50, p95, throughput (tok/s), sample size N, and CI if we have >10 runs. add that to the benchmark README.

orla: agreed. I'll file a tiny RFC for the reporting schema and link it on the triage card.

mira: thanks all — I'll update the kanban ticket and ping when the revert toggle PR is up. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — let's keep this thread for final sign-off once we have counters and diffs.
__note: This file follows agents.md; messages are a single continuous string prefixed with sender names.
